description.narrative:
Transparency International Anti-Corruption Center - Armenia (TIAC) har ansökt till Sida om finansiering på totalt 7 100 000 SEK för att genomföra projektet "Institutional Support Grant" under perioden 2021-2023.
Insatsen syftar till att genom kärnstöd till TIAC stödja pågående ansträngningar för att främja god samhällsstyrning och antikorruptionspolicy genom följande mål; 1) policy och lagändring för att säkerställa transparent och ansvarsfull styrning, 2) beteendeförändring för att öka medborgarnas intolerans mot korruption; 3) uppsökande och medvetandehöjande för att påverka policyn och beteendeförändringar; 4) organisationsutveckling.
Stödet, som planeras att tillhandahållas i form av kärnstöd kommer att syfta till att möjliggöra för TIAC att bidra till Armeniens demokratiska utveckling. Insatsen kommer enbart att genomföras av TIAC, utan vidareförmedling av medel till tredje part.

Transparency International Anti-corruption Center - Armenia (TIAC) has applied to Sida for funding of 7 100 000 SEK, to carry out "Institutional Support Grant" project during the period of 2021-2023.
The intervention aims to provide core support to TIAC’s ongoing efforts in promoting good governance and anti-corruption policies through the following objectives; 1) policy and legislative change to ensure transparent and accountable governance; 2) behavioral change to enhance intolerance of citizens toward corruption; 3) outreach and awareness raising to influence the policy and behavior changes; 4) organizational development.
The support, which is planned to be provided in the form of core support, will enable TIAC to contribute to Armenia´s democratic development. The intervention will be solely implemented by TIAC, with no forwarding of funds to third parties.

The project strengthenes anti-corruption monitoring and reporting mechanisms, generating credible evidence and increasing the use of data in public discourse. At the same time, findings reveal deeper systemic issues and resistance within institutions, highlighting a wider gap between formal commitments and actual practice than initially anticipated.
Civic engagement and public participation improved through awareness-raising activities and platforms enabling citizens to report and discuss corruption-related issues. Outreach efforts have helped broaden participation, including among groups previously less engaged, though sustaining active involvement remains a challenge.
Advocacy achieved solid visibility and contributed to shaping public narratives on corruption, with targeted outputs drawing attention among key audiences. Increased exposure also led to pushback from affected stakeholders, indicating both relevance and sensitivity of the work. Advocacy also put pressure on institutions and contributed to incremental policy discussions and reform processes. With some emerging opportunites for dialogue, progress toward concrete institutional change remains somewhat slow due to political and structural constraints.
From the organizational development aspect, the project demonstrates strong technical competence and stable implementation, with continued improvements in analytical, monitoring, and communication systems, allowing for more strategic and adaptive interventions.
Showcase results
Contributing to anti-corruption policy reform: Implementation gaps persisted in Armenias anti-corruption strategy, including weak coordination between institutions and insufficient monitoring of reform commitments. TIAC actively participated in policy consultations, submitted recommendations to draft legislation and national strategies, and monitored government compliance with anti-corruption commitments, as well as conducted assessment of the Corruption Prevention Commission (CPC), providing a clearer understanding of the institutions strengths and weaknesses. The assessment laid the groundwork for targeted institutional improvements aimed at enhancing the CPCs effectiveness. It evaluated the CPC's compliance with the requirements derived from the UN "Convention against Corruption" and the principles set out in the Jakarta Declaration, based on which TIAC presented 48 recommendations aimed at enhancing the establishment and operational effectiveness of the CPC. Civil society engagement improved the quality and inclusiveness of anti-corruption policymaking. TIACs contributions strengthened institutional accountability and reinforced Armenias alignment with international anti-corruption standards.
Monitoring public procurement to prevent corruption risks: Public procurement remains one of the sectors most vulnerable to corruption, particularly at local levels where oversight capacity is limited and transparency practices are inconsistently applied. TIAC actively engaged youth in municipal monitoring activities by launching a dedicated youth monitoring initiative. Following a two-day intensive training for 14 young monitors on procurement legislation, budget analysis, monitoring methodologies, the participants were engaged in the first phase of monitoring and assessed 70 renovated or newly built playgrounds and sports grounds across all 12 administrative districts of Yerevan through procurement analysis, field visits, photo and video documentation, and surveys of over 750 residents. The monitoring increased transparency in procurement processes and strengthened external oversight. Authorities became more responsive to civil society findings, contributing to improved compliance with procurement standards and reduced opportunities for misuse of public funds.
Enhancing whistleblower protection and reporting mechanisms: Although Armenia has a legal framework for whistleblower protection, awareness and practical implementation remained weak. Citizens and public servants were reluctant to report corruption due to fear of retaliation and lack of confidence in protection mechanisms. TIAC conducted awareness campaigns, legal monitoring, and advocacy to strengthen implementation of whistleblower protection provisions. Legal consultations and guidance were provided to potential whistleblowers, and gaps in enforcement were documented and communicated to responsible authorities. Improved awareness and practical support increased confidence in reporting mechanisms. By strengthening protective frameworks and public understanding, TIAC contributed to a safer enabling environment for accountability and anti-corruption reporting.
Strengthening integrity mechanisms in local government: Despite ongoing public sector reforms, Armenian municipalities continue to face systemic corruption risks, weak internal control mechanisms, and limited citizen trust. Anti-corruption compliance tools existed in legislation but were inconsistently applied at local level. Through TIACs technical support, selected municipalities introduced and operationalized integrity tools, including anti-corruption action plans, risk assessment mechanisms, and internal reporting procedures. Municipal officials received targeted training on compliance standards and transparency requirements. Local administrations shifted from ad hoc compliance toward more structured integrity management systems. The strengthened preventive mechanisms contribute to reducing corruption risks, increasing accountability, and rebuilding public trust in local governance institutions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
